label: around the delimiter in long sequences (last original token, <DEL>, first copy step; L>=8)
explanation: Fires only in a narrow window around the original-to-copy transition: the last original token (t=L-1), the <DEL> step, and the first copy-input step (t=L+1, input = orig(0), output = orig(1)), and almost only for long sequences (L=9 holds 74% of mass, L=8 21%, nothing for L<=5). The strongest activations come at t=L+1 when L=9, and they are higher when the first token is u/m/b/n/1/j. It never fires at t<6 or in the later copy phase (recall_idx>=3). The window predicate captures about 93% of activation mass but has low precision (~0.11): within the window it fires on only a minority of steps, and which ones depends on token content (first token, digit count) in ways that no simple rule captured (adding first_tok gives F1 0.39).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: u, v, n, j, 1, k; least: 0, l, d, s) and the current input token, by step (t=7: m, 0, b, 1; t=8: m, 0, b, w; t=11: 1, j, m, n); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=8, t=8.
